chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Basir said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying to him: 'Is it permissible for a Muslim man to marry a muqatabah (female slave who has agreed to pay for her freedom) who has already paid half of her manumission contract?' He said, and he said: 'If her master, at the time he contracted her manumission, stipulated upon her that if she became unable (to pay the rest), she would return to slavery, then her marriage is not valid until she pays all that is upon her.'

key_terms.مُكَاتَبَة: A slave who has contracted with their master to pay a specific sum for their freedom

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a female slave who has paid half her manumission price?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal status of a muqatabah (slave woman who has contracted for her freedom) by linking the validity of her marriage to the specific terms of her manumission contract. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that her legal capacity to marry is contingent upon her complete financial independence from her master, ensuring that the condition of 'return to slavery' is fully resolved. This underscores the importance of contractual stipulations in determining the transition from slavery to free status in Islamic family law.
